points.point: The strongest infrastructure opportunity is mmWave / higher-frequency and early-6G network analysis, where the MWC2025 network-infrastructure deck lists ZNA up to 67 GHz and ZNA67EXT up to 110 GHz.
points.label: missing
points.why: does not mention mmWave/early-6G MWC2025 evidence, ZNA 67 GHz, or ZNA67EXT 110 GHz

points.point: Beamforming / Massive MIMO component and accuracy verification is a named VNA opportunity, addressed by the R&S ZNBT multiport network analyzer up to 40 GHz with simultaneous measurement on up to 24 ports in one instrument.
points.label: missing
points.why: no ZNBT, 40 GHz, 24-port simultaneous measurement, or Massive MIMO verification evidence

points.point: The ZNA's multi-source, multi-receiver architecture supports antenna array tests and antenna test systems with true parallel and coherent data acquisition, which underpins the active-antenna/array opportunity.
points.label: missing
points.why: no ZNA multi-source/multi-receiver, true parallel, or coherent acquisition support

points.point: For satellite communication payloads and components, the ZNA is positioned for group delay of frequency converters without LO access using a two-tone technique, i.e. component-level testing.
points.label: partial
points.why: mentions satellite/LEO RF-front-end characterization with ZNA, but omits payload frequency-converter group delay, no-LO access, and two-tone technique

points.point: In the Taiwan satellite supply-chain mapping, VNAs (ZNA / ZNB3000) are mapped to antenna G/T measurement, and the ZNA also to ground stations, UT and communication-module players.
points.label: partial
points.why: mentions satellite ground equipment and user terminals generally, but not Taiwan mapping to antenna G/T, ground stations, UT, and communication modules with ZNA/ZNB3000

points.point: Satellite user-terminal test flows list a VNA for phased-array calibration, with the ZNA named alongside the incumbent Keysight PNA-X.

points.point: Antenna high-isolation measurement and OTA passive testing in the Taiwan UAV wireless chain is mapped to the R&S ZNB3000.
